fields.note: 5.1: for i in steps.size() visits every index; beat % steps.size() wraps the playhead.

why: 5.1 is its first need: the playhead counts through steps.size() and wraps by it.

fields.note: 5.5: flip() builds each row again from its far end, one append at a time; 5.8 appends bodies.

why: 5.5 is its first need: flip() rebuilds a row with append().

fields.note: 5.3: the 4 x 4 source is the first grid of chapter 5, sixteen cells each holding a palette number; 5.1's row of steps calls its boxes squares. 13.1 gives a cell its state and returns to it.

why: 5.1 has one row of steps, not a grid; the 4 x 4 source of 5.3 is the first grid whose places hold a state.

fields.def: An array of colours, read by a number.
fields.note: 5.2: palette[value] turns a 0 or 1 into a colour; from 5.3 on source holds palette numbers, as the halls do.

why: The sketch's 5.2 title and idea; every later section of chapter 5 reads palette[source[z][x]]. A term that matters is a type.

fields.note: 5.1: $Supplied.note() sounds the step the playhead reads; the AudioStreamPlayer inside is never opened.

why: 5.1's code has to sound a step: the supplied part needed a call and a stub, as line() has.

fields.def: The floor square under the mouse, as an array: x, z.
fields.note: 5.6: hover the patterned floor; at[0] % 4 and at[1] % 4 find the cell of source a square reads. An array, not a Vector2i: chapter 5 keeps y for up, so a floor square is x and z, and Vector2i would call z y. The ray inside is never opened.

why: Chapter 5 paints nothing by hand in 5.5 (it writes into source by code before drawing); the first section that points at a square is 5.6, the floor that reads source. The stub answers the sketch's floor square [10, 1].

fields.def: A strip of floor your figures walk along.
fields.note: 5.8: a supplied scene dropped on the top node, a stage only; the walk itself is the student's code (position.z += delta, turn by turn).

why: 5.8 borrows it as the stage the bodies walk on; it needed a file the student can drop, as counter_panel.tscn is.

fields.def: How the hall repeats the pattern on the skirt.
fields.note: chapter 5 writer, 2 October 2026: no longer supplied. 5.8 dresses the skirts with the ImageTexture of 5.6, so nothing borrows the hall's shader repeat; it needs UV (12.1). A supplied part must have a section, so it is a missing concept until chapter 12 teaches it or it is deleted.

why: 5.8 does not need it (the skirt wears the 5.6 ImageTexture); a supplied part cannot be missing, so its kind changes. Delete it if chapter 12 has no use for it.

fields.def: Makes a blank `Image`, so wide and so high.

why: 5.6 makes the 16 x 16 Image the floor wears.

fields.def: An `Image` kind: red, green and blue at each place.

why: create_empty() needs a format; 5.6 uses Image.FORMAT_RGB8.
5.6 turns the Image into a texture with ImageTexture.create_from_image().

fields.def: The texture a material wears as its colour.

why: 5.6 puts the texture on the floor's material.

fields.def: How a texture is drawn between its places.
fields.note: TEXTURE_FILTER_NEAREST is its one value in the course: a 16 x 16 picture on a 16 metre floor stays sixteen sharp squares a side, not a blur.

why: Without it the 16 x 16 picture is blurred across the floor and the cells cannot be read.

fields.def: A flat square mesh lying down, 2 metres a side.

why: 5.6's floor wears the picture; a BoxMesh would spread it over six faces.

fields.def: A flat square mesh standing up, 1 metre a side.

why: 5.7's four panels stand up, as in the chapter's opening picture.
Look's def says palette, which chapter 5 makes an entry (5.2); a def's terms are its dependencies.
